excluded_from_unit_coverage.rationale: The Iced view layer, the application loop in lib.rs and the binary edge require a display server and are exercised by the end-to-end target instead of unit tests.

measurement_configuration.mechanism: cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 reads no configuration file of its own and accepts the exclusion only through the --ignore-filename-regex flag, so the exclusion is injected with the LLVM_COV_FLAGS environment variable, which cargo-llvm-cov forwards verbatim to llvm-cov export. Cargo's [env] configuration is applied only to build scripts, rustc, cargo run and cargo test, never to external subcommands, so the variable cannot be carried by .cargo/config.toml.
measurement_configuration.report_contents: coverage/lcov.info carries only src/core/** and src/platform/** records
measurement_configuration.portability_note: The recorded regex is separator-agnostic: [\\/] matches the forward slash llvm-cov emits on POSIX and the backslash it emits on Windows, so a single env value excludes the same set (src/main.rs, src/lib.rs, src/ui/**) on both CI legs. The earlier POSIX-only spelling (^|/)src/((main|lib)\.rs|ui/) matches that identical set on Linux but would miss src\ui\... on Windows.
measurement_configuration.ci_note: The CI coverage stage wires the same separator-agnostic scope into its cargo llvm-cov invocation and enforces the gate with --fail-under-lines 90 --fail-under-functions 90 on both matrix operating systems, so the gate is enforced outside the capture run as well. The excluded set (src/main.rs, src/lib.rs, src/ui/**) and the 90 % threshold are identical to the capture configuration.
measurement_configuration.branches_note: branches reads 100 over a 0/0 denominator: every record of the scoped LCOV report carries BRF:0 and BRH:0 because the crate produces no branch counters, so 100 % is vacuous and must not be read as real branch coverage. Treat branches as not measured; only lines and functions are gated. statements is null because the LCOV format carries no statement counter.

baseline.note: The 90% gate applies to core/ and platform/ pure logic, which measures 96.93% lines and 96.34% functions (unit_testable_scope.status = at_or_above_target) and is the metric range recorded against the 90% thresholds in openspec/changes/<change>/logs/evidence.json. The overall project percentage (96.31% lines, 95.75% functions) counts the display-bound files and is reported as a trend rather than as the gated metric: the Iced UI layer, the application loop and the binary edge cannot be unit-tested without a display server, so their coverage depends on the end-to-end run and moves independently of the gate. The 90% threshold is never lowered; the excluded files are removed by the measurement configuration recorded under measurement_configuration. Figures come from the current HEAD run: measured_* counts the whole crate, unit_testable_scope counts the gated subset, and the manifest records the capture run it executed.
baseline.sonarqube_gate_note: The SonarQube quality gate reports PASS because the gate conditions configured on the server carry no hard 90% coverage threshold during the bootstrap phase; the enforceable 90% gate is the CI Run coverage stage, and coverage is otherwise tracked as a trend until feature work begins (design D6). The 90% target applies to the unit-testable scope recorded in unit_testable_scope (96.93% lines, 96.34% functions). sonar-project.properties declares analysis inputs only and holds no gate threshold, so the gate result is not evidence that the overall project percentage met the target. Rationale documented in docs/project-context.md.
